cs.label: [section] Cíl předmětu a studijní výstupy:
cs.content: Cílem kurzu je prozkoumat komplexní vztah společnosti a životního prostředí. Tento kurz bude zkoumat, jak lidské chování a sociální struktury ovlivňují životní prostředí, stejně jako to, jak environmentální problémy ovlivňují sociální systémy a nerovnosti.

en.label: Prerequisites:
en.content: Environmental Protection and Conservation or Sociology or Introduction to Environmentalistics
Introduction to Environmental Sociology (allowance 4/4)

en.label: a.
en.content: Overview of environmental sociology and its key concepts, theories, and research methods
The Social Construction of Nature (allowance 2/2)

en.label: a.
en.content: Explore the ways in which our ideas about nature are shaped by culture, history, and politics
Sustainable Development and Consumption (allowance 2/2)

en.label: a.
en.content: The role of consumption in environmental degradation and the concept of sustainable consumption
Environmental Movements and Social Change (allowance 4/4)

en.label: a.
en.content: Historical and contemporary environmental movements and their impact on social change
Political Ecology (allowance 2/2)

en.label: a.
en.content: Exploring the ways in which power relations shape environmental decision-making and outcome
Environmental Justice (allowance 2/2)

en.label: a.
en.content: The concept of environmental justice and its relationship with race, class, and gender
Environmental Ethics (allowance 2/2)

en.label: a.
en.content: Different ethical frameworks for understanding human-environment relationships and their implications for environmental policy
Social Relations to Animals (allowance 2/2)

en.label: a.
en.content: Post-anthropocentric sociological approach, which attributes social agency to beings other than members of the biological species homo sapiens
Ecological Modernization (allowance 2/2)

en.label: a.
en.content: Can economic growth and environmental protection be reconciled through technological innovation and policy reform?
Environmental Sociology and the Anthropocene (allowance 2/2)

en.label: a.
en.content: The concept of the Anthropocene and its implications for environmental sociology
Environmental Education and Communication (allowance 2/2)

en.label: a.
en.content: The role of education and communication in promoting environmental awareness and action

en.label: [section] Aim of the course and learning outcomes:
en.content: The aim of the study course is to explore the complex relationship between society and the environment. This course will examine how human behaviour and social structures impact the environment, as well as how environmental issues affect social systems and inequality.

en.label: [section] Course content:
en.content: 1.Introduction to Environmental Sociology (allowance 4/4) a.Overview of environmental sociology and its key concepts, theories, and research methods2.The Social Construction of Nature (allowance 2/2) a.Explore the ways in which our ideas about nature are shaped by culture, history, and politics3.Sustainable Development and Consumption (allowance 2/2) a.The role of consumption in environmental degradation and the concept of sustainable consumption4.Environmental Movements and Social Change (allowance 4/4) a.Historical and contemporary environmental movements and their impact on social change5.Political Ecology (allowance 2/2) a.Exploring the ways in which power relations shape environmental decision-making and outcome6.Environmental Justice (allowance 2/2) a.The concept of environmental justice and its relationship with race, class, and gender7.Environmental Ethics (allowance 2/2) a.Different ethical frameworks for understanding human-environment relationships and their implications for environmental policy8.Social Relations to Animals (allowance 2/2) a.Post-anthropocentric sociological approach, which attributes social agency to beings other than members of the biological species homo sapiens9.Ecological Modernization (allowance 2/2) a.Can economic growth and environmental protection be reconciled through technological innovation and policy reform?10.Environmental Sociology and the Anthropocene (allowance 2/2) a.The concept of the Anthropocene and its implications for environmental sociology11.Environmental Education and Communication (allowance 2/2) a.The role of education and communication in promoting environmental awareness and action

en.label: [section] Assessment methods:
en.content: Credit: 1. Review of literature from research papers on selected topics and oral presentations 2. Group projects and presentations that demonstrate students' ability to apply concepts and theories learned in the course to real-world environmental problems. Exam: Knowledge of concepts discussed in lectures.
